transcript.en: Scientists believe that a majority of the earth's bird population migrate in some fashion or other.
transcript.zh: 科学家认为，地球上大多数鸟类种群都以某种方式迁徙。

transcript.en: Some travel seasonally for relatively short distances, such as birds that move from their winter habitats in lowlands to mountain tops for the summers.
transcript.zh: 有些是季节性的迁徙，是相对较短的距离，例如鸟类从低地的冬季栖息地移动到山顶去过夏天。

transcript.en: Others, like the Arctic Tern, travel more than 25,000 miles seasonally between the northern and southern poles.
transcript.zh: 其他物种，如北极燕鸥，在北极和南极之间季节性穿越超过25,000英里。

transcript.en: Bird migration has been studied over many centuries through a variety of observations.
transcript.zh: 几个世纪以来，科学家通过各种观察，对鸟类迁徙进行了研究。

transcript.en: But until relatively recently, where birds went to in the winter was considered something of a mystery.
transcript.zh: 但直到最近，鸟类在冬天去的地方还被认为是一个谜。

transcript.en: The lack of modern science and technology led to many theories that we now recognize as error-filled and even somewhat amusing.
transcript.zh: 现代现代科技的缺乏产生的很多理论，在我们现在看来是充满错误甚至有些可笑的。

transcript.en: Take hibernation theory for example -two thousand years ago, it was commonly believed that when birds left an area, they went underwater to hibernate in the seas and oceans.
transcript.zh: 以冬眠理论为例——两千年前，人们普遍认为，当鸟类离开一个地区时，它们会潜入水下，在海洋中冬眠。

transcript.en: Another theory for the regular appearance and disappearance of birds was that they spent winter hidden in mud till the weather changed and food became abundant again.
transcript.zh: 另一种关于鸟类经常出现和消失的理论是，它们躲在泥泞中度过冬天，直到天气变化，食物再次变得丰富。

transcript.en: The theory that some birds hibernate persisted until experiments were done on caged birds in the 1940s
transcript.zh: 一些鸟类冬眠的理论一直持续到20世纪40年代，对笼中鸟类进行实验，

transcript.en: which demonstrated that birds have no hibernation instinct.
transcript.zh: 该实验表明鸟类没有冬眠本能。

transcript.en: One of the earliest naturalists and philosophers from ancient Greece was Aristotle
transcript.zh: 古希腊最早的自然主义者和哲学家之一亚里士多德

transcript.en: who was the first writer to discuss the disappearance and reappearance of some bird species at certain times of year.
transcript.zh: 是第一个讨论某些鸟类在一年中某些时候消失和重新出现的作者。

transcript.en: He developed the theory of transmutation, the seasonal change of one species into another, by observing redstarts and robins.
transcript.zh: 他发展了嬗变理论，即一个物种到另一个物种的季节性变化，通过观察红尾鸲和知更鸟。

transcript.en: He observed that in the autumn,small birds called 'redstarts' began to lose their feathers,
transcript.zh: 他观察到，在秋天，被称为“红尾鸲”的小鸟开始失去羽毛，

transcript.en: which convinced Aristotle that they changed into robins for the winter, and back into redstarts in the summer.
transcript.zh: 这让亚里士多德相信，它们在冬天变成了知更鸟，在夏天又变回了红尾鸲。

transcript.en: These assumptions are understandable given that this pair of species are similar in shape,
transcript.zh: 这些假设是可以理解的，因为这对物种在形状上是相似的，

transcript.en: but are a classic example of an incorrect interpretation based on correct observations.
transcript.zh: 但是这是基于正确观察的错误解释的典型例子。

transcript.en: The most bizarre theory was put forward by an English amateur scientist, Charles Morton, in the seventeenth century.
transcript.zh: 最奇怪的理论是由英国业余科学家查尔斯·莫顿（Charles Morton）在十七世纪提出的。

transcript.en: He wrote a surprisingly well-regarded paper claiming  that birds migrate to the moon and back every year.
transcript.zh: 他写了一篇出人意料的备受推崇的论文，声称鸟类每年都会迁移到月球并返回。

transcript.en: He came to this conclusion as the only logical explanation for the total disappearance of some species.
transcript.zh: 他得出这个结论是基于某些物种完全消失的唯一合乎逻辑的解释。

transcript.en: One of the key moments in the development of migration theory came in 1822 when a white stork was shot in Germany.
transcript.zh: 迁徙理论发展的关键时刻之一发生在1822年，当时一只白鹳在德国被射杀。

transcript.en: This particular stork made history because of the long spear in its neck which incredibly had not killed it
transcript.zh: 这只特殊的鹳创造了历史，因为它脖子上的长矛没有杀死它 -

transcript.en: everyone immediately realised this spear was definitely not European.
transcript.zh: 每个人都立即意识到这把矛绝对不是欧洲人的。

transcript.en: It turned out to be a spear from a tribe in Central Africa.
transcript.zh: 原来是来自中非一个部落的长矛。

transcript.en: This was a truly defining moment in the history of ornithology because it was the first evidence that storks spend their winters in sub-Saharan Africa.
transcript.zh: 这是鸟类学史上一个真正具有决定性意义的时刻，因为这是鹳在撒哈拉以南非洲过冬的第一个证据。

transcript.en: You can still see the 'arrow stork' in the Zoological Collection of the University of Rostock in Germany.
transcript.zh: 您仍然可以在德国罗斯托克大学的动物学收藏中看到“箭鹳”。

transcript.en: People gradually became aware that European birds moved south in autumn and north in summer
transcript.zh: 人们逐渐意识到欧洲鸟类在秋天向南移动，在夏天向北移动，

transcript.en: but didn't know much about it until the practice of catching birds and putting rings on their legs became established.
transcript.zh: 但这一点直到鸟类捕捉 并在鸟类腿上套环后才被真正了解。

transcript.en: Before this, very little information was available about the actual destinations of particular species and how they travelled there.
transcript.zh: 在此之前，特定物种的信息很少，有关于实际目的地 以及它们如何飞到那里。

transcript.en: People speculated that larger birds provided a kind of taxi service for smaller birds by carrying them on their backs.
transcript.zh: 人们推测，较大的鸟类通过背着较小的鸟类为较小的鸟类提供了一种出租车服务。

transcript.en: This idea came about because it seemed impossible that small birds weighing only a few grams could fly over vast oceans.
transcript.zh: 这个想法之所以产生，是因为只有几克重的小鸟似乎不可能飞越浩瀚的海洋。

transcript.en: This idea was supported by observations of bird behaviour such as the harassment of larger birds by smaller birds.
transcript.zh: 这个想法得到了鸟类行为观察的支持，例如较小的鸟类对大型鸟类的骚扰。

transcript.en: The development of bird ringing,  by a Danish schoolteacher, Hans Christian Cornelius Mortensen, made many discoveries possible.
transcript.zh: 鸟类套环的发展，由丹麦学校教师汉斯·克里斯蒂安·科尼利厄斯（Hans Christian Cornelius）撰写，使许多发现成为可能。

transcript.en: This is still common practice today and relies upon what is known as 'recovery'  this is when ringed birds are found dead in the place they have migrated to, and identified.
transcript.zh: 这在今天仍然很常见，并且依赖于所谓的“恢复”— 这是当套环鸟被发现死在它们迁徙到的地方 并被识别出来时。

transcript.en: Huge amounts of data were gathered in the early part of the twentieth century and for the first time in history people understood where birds actually went to in winter.
transcript.zh: 在二十世纪初收集了大量的数据，人们在历史上第一次了解了鸟类在冬天的实际去向。

transcript.en: In 1931, an atlas was published showing where the most common species of European birds migrated to.
transcript.zh: 1931年，出版了一本地图集，显示了最常见的欧洲鸟类迁徙到哪里。

transcript.en: More recent theories about bird migration ...
transcript.zh: 更多关于鸟类迁徙的最新理论...
